papers.title: Effect of Imbalance Settlement Design on Risk-Averse Aggregator Scheduling: A CVaR-Based Parametric Study
papers.abstract: Electricity market settlement rules shape the financial exposure that energy aggregators face when generation deviates from contracted positions, yet their interaction with Conditional-Value-at-Risk-based risk-aversion strategies in aggregator scheduling remains unexplored. This paper studies how the design of imbalance penalty rules influences optimal risk-aversion in a stochastic unit commitment framework for a network-constrained aggregator operating a diversified portfolio of generation resources. Four settlement regimes are defined: a regime with halved deviation penalty rates, a baseline regime matching empirical market data, a strict regime with doubled penalty rates, and a self-balancing regime that prohibits contracted day-ahead exchange. A parametric sweep of the risk aversion weight λ at a fixed confidence level α is conducted on a modified IEEE 9-bus test system using 50 stochastic scenarios. To resolve the transition between the discrete regimes, a finer penalty sweep is also performed. Results show that stricter settlement designs increase tail-risk exposure at the risk-neutral baseline, while the benefit of risk weighting is largest under the strict and self-balancing regimes. Battery energy storage throughput responds to λ under market-participatory regimes but becomes invariant under self-balancing constraints. The findings provide quantitative guidance on how settlement regime should inform aggregator risk management strategy.
